oauthFit.reason: Standard authorization_code flow (OAuth v2) with a real consent/install step; instant for a single workspace, review only required for public Marketplace distribution.

decision.question: Will this run in your own workspace only, or get listed for any workspace to install?

options.name: Single workspace
pickWhen: Building for your own team or workspace
You want to start testing immediately
options.tradeoff: Instant, no review — but the app can't be installed by other workspaces.

options.name: Slack Marketplace (public distribution)
pickWhen: Any Slack workspace should be able to install your app
options.tradeoff: Requires 10+ active installs before you can even submit, a two-phase review that can take up to ~12 weeks total, and restricts which scopes you can request.

decision.recommendation: Start with a single-workspace install to build and test. Pursue Marketplace listing only once you have real usage — the install threshold and review timeline make it a late-stage step, not a launch blocker.

summary: Creating a Slack app and installing it to your own workspace is instant with no review. Listing it in the Slack Marketplace for anyone to install is a different story — it requires 10+ active installs before you can even submit, then a two-phase review that can take up to roughly 12 weeks.

evidence.note: Official docs don't state a hands-on setup time; the estimate above is based on the number of required steps (create app, configure scopes, set redirect URI, install), not a documented figure.

paths.name: Single workspace (your own)
paths.notes: Install to the workspace you created the app in — instant, no review.

paths.name: Slack Marketplace (public distribution)
paths.wait: Up to 10 business days for a preliminary review, then up to 10 weeks for the functional review on new submissions (6 weeks for resubmissions) — cannot be expedited
paths.notes: Requires 10+ active installs (used within the last 28 days) before you can even submit, sustained throughout the review.

cost.value: Free — the Slack Web API has no usage-based or per-call pricing.
cost.notes: A Slack workspace (free or paid tier) is required to develop against, but workspace subscription pricing is separate from API usage. No metered usage cap to run out of — only per-method rate limits apply.

rateLimits.value: No per-call charges. Subject to per-method rate limits (tiered, roughly 1 to 100+ requests/minute depending on the method), regardless of workspace plan.

prerequisites.text: A Slack workspace to develop in — your own, or a development sandbox.
A publicly reachable HTTPS redirect URI. Slack rejects plain http:// and any URL containing an anchor (#).

If targeting Marketplace listing: the app must already be installed on 10 or more active workspaces (used within the last 28 days) before submission, sustained throughout the review, and fully tested end-to-end including uninstall on a non-development workspace.

minimum.why: Send messages as the app's bot identity — the most common agent integration need.

optional.why: List public channels, if the agent needs to discover where to post.
Look up workspace members, if the agent needs to mention or DM specific users.

modes.name: Bot scopes (scope parameter)
modes.whenToUse: The app's own identity and permissions — use for most integrations.

modes.name: User scopes (user_scope parameter)
modes.whenToUse: Acting on behalf of the installing user specifically, rather than as the app's own bot identity.

steps.title: Create the app
steps.description: Go to api.slack.com/apps, click 'Create New App', choose 'From scratch' or 'From an app manifest', and select the workspace to develop in.
steps.agentAssist: Can pre-fill the app name and manifest once a session is authenticated.

steps.title: Configure OAuth scopes
steps.description: Under OAuth & Permissions, add bot scopes (the app's own identity and permissions, via the scope parameter) and/or user scopes (acting on behalf of a user, via user_scope) depending on what the integration needs.
steps.agentAssist: Can pre-fill the minimum scopes needed for the integration.

steps.title: Set the redirect URI
steps.description: Add the HTTPS redirect URI under OAuth & Permissions. It must exactly match — or be a subdirectory of — the URL sent in the authorization request.
steps.agentAssist: Can pre-fill Composio's redirect URI directly.

steps.title: Install to your workspace
steps.description: Click 'Install to Workspace' to generate a token and start testing immediately — no review needed for this step.

blockers.fix: It must be HTTPS, contain no anchor (#), and exactly match or be a subdirectory of a URL configured under OAuth & Permissions.

blockers.problem: App can't be installed by other workspaces.
blockers.fix: Expected before the app is approved for public distribution — until then it's restricted to the workspace it was created in. The team parameter only becomes a hint (not a restriction) once the app is distributed.

blockers.problem: Marketplace submission rejected before review even starts.
blockers.fix: Reach 10+ active installs (used within the last 28 days) and keep that threshold through the whole review. Fully test the install, setup, and uninstall flow on a non-development workspace first.

agentCanDo: Find the app-creation form and current OAuth & Permissions fields
Pre-fill the app name, scopes, and redirect URI
Check Marketplace prerequisites — install count, uninstall testing — before submission
Draft the Marketplace review submission text
humanMustDo: Create the app and configure OAuth scopes and redirect URI in the Slack dashboard
If pursuing Marketplace listing: reach the 10-install threshold and handle the review submission
composioHandoff: Paste the client ID and client secret into Composio, with Composio's callback URL registered as the OAuth redirect URI — Composio manages the authorization flow, token exchange, and refresh from there.
